# CLAIMs with `line` `readiness`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

**Readiness and slack** — what it takes to keep, reach and pay for capacities whose value lies in rare circumstances — readiness as response capability, slack and reconfiguration slack as different reserves, the resource threshold of a transition and its obstructions, and budget rules that remove options no one chose to give up (ADR-073). When transient support can be withdrawn is a line of its own (ADR-087).

| [CLAIM-572](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-572.md) v3 | When observing and acting draw on one budget, the cheapest readiness always buys a whole prefix of the probes and stops where a probe lowers the response budget, the splits a fixed budget affords can be disconnected, so shifting resources gradually from response to observation can pass through splits that are not ready, and stopping when the next probe does not pay can miss the optimum | The assistant's, on the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to investigate organizations whose observing and acting draw on one budget. The organization stands in a posture; each circumstance has acceptable configurations, each reachable from the posture at some cost; probes bought in a fixed order refine what it can tell apart. The acting budget it needs, a*(o), is the largest, over what it cannot tell apart at o, of the cheapest configuration acceptable throughout. With o + a ≤ B, three things follow. The least total is reached at a probe cost, never between. | [CLAIM-580](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-580.md) v2 | The transition threshold is stable under error in the resource function: if an estimate of the requirement is within ε of the true one at every configuration, the estimated threshold is within ε of the true one, and an underestimate anywhere can only lower it while an overestimate can only raise it | The assistant's own proposition, offered at the owner's invitation on 2026-11-05. The threshold of [CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md) is the least, over admissible paths, of each path's peak requirement, and both the peak and the least move by at most the largest error in the requirement. So a planner who knows each configuration's cost to within ε knows a transition's threshold to within ε, and its reconfiguration slack to within 2ε. The error is also one-sided in a useful way: overestimating only raises the threshold, and underestimating anywhere can only lower it, possibly by opening a cheaper path that does not exist. It is the zero-dimensional case of the stability of sublevel-set persistence that Mirth et al. use. With several resources the same argument bounds the set of sufficient budgets coordinate by coordinate. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |

| [CLAIM-598](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-598.md) v3 | Whether more of every resource raises, leaves or lowers the chance that an assembly reaches its target depends, at each branch point, on whether the competing steps consume further resource: a branch whose steps all consume alike is unchanged by uniform abundance, and one where the wrong step consumes and the right one does not is made worse by it, as Majikes et al. report for a single DNA origami fold that excess staples block | The assistant's, from A's second synthesis on DNA origami, pasted by the owner on 2026-11-05. In A's branching model of assembly, the chance of reaching the target is a product of branch choices, each a ratio of the rates of the competing steps. If supply rises uniformly by λ, a step that consumes a further unit, binding another molecule, speeds up by λ, while a step within what is already assembled does not. So a choice is unchanged by abundance when its competing steps consume alike, and shifted when they differ. More of everything hurts where the wrong step consumes and the right one does not. Majikes et al. 2021 find exactly this for one fold of a DNA origami: two staple molecules can each take one end and block it, and the folded share j/(j + S₀) falls as staple excess rises. A's remark that "The relevant resource isn't always total abundance" is thus made exact. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) v4 | Where an organization's capacity is learned by doing the work it serves, and decays with disuse, outside supply that does the work first lowers the capacity kept, and the longer it does all of it the longer recovery takes once it stops, while supply that covers only what the organization cannot yet do leaves its learning untouched, so what decides dependence is the order in which supply and capacity are used, not the amount of supply | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to look to aid and development for theory on how aid-dependent organizations become self-sufficient. [CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md) holds an outside supply that repairs the organization and leaves its own capacity alone. The readings say aid does not leave it alone: it does the work the capacity is learned from. Moss, Pettersson and van de Walle cite Kaldor, that a state leaves aid dependency as it "learns how to tax". Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's 1999 model already has taxing experience built by revenue collected and decaying with time, and capacity kept lower the more aid finances. Moore says raising revenue keeps a state's machinery alive at the grassroots. Ostrom et al. find recipients losing skill and rebuilding plants they did not maintain, and Andrews, Pritchett and Woolcock find capability stagnating under aid. In a model where capacity grows with the work done and decays with disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), aid that does a share A of the work first holds capacity at λ(1 − A)/(λ(1 − A) + μ): with λ = 1, μ = 0.3, 0.769 without aid, 0.625 at A = 0.5, 0.25 at 0.9 and none at full substitution. After full substitution for 10, 20 and 40 time units, meeting demand takes 3.8, 6.4 and 11.4 units once aid stops, because the work an organization can do is capped by its capacity, so it regrows from a seed. Aid used after capacity, covering only what it cannot yet do, keeps service whole and leaves capacity to grow as if there were no aid. The first point is Azam et al.'s; the second and third are not in their paper. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-632](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-632.md) v3 | Records kept of each capacity a response needs bound a reserve's readiness for a contingency between the sum of their probabilities less one less their number and the weakest of them, and identify it only when the capacities' dependence is known, so for any verdict that rises with readiness they can refute a required readiness when the weakest capacity falls below it and certify it only when the capacities' shortfalls together stay within its margin, leaving the band between to joint evidence such as a deadline-bound exercise; where capacities only decay between record and need, a refutation outlasts the record and a certification does not | [QUESTION-395](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-395.md) asks which observations tell a warranted reserve of specialized capability from wasteful redundancy, and which of them identify readiness ([TERM-115](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-115.md)) and which only bound it. [CLAIM-587](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-587.md) makes a response the conjunction of complementary capacities. So records kept per capacity (rosters, training assessments, equipment availability, turnout times) fix only the marginals, which bound readiness by the Fréchet inequalities and do not identify it. A record can refute a required readiness through the weakest capacity, and can certify it only when the shortfalls sum within the margin; between those, only joint evidence decides. With [CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)'s decay, a certification expires with the record's age and a refutation does not. The inference leans mainly on [CLAIM-587](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-587.md); its integrating work is joining it with [TERM-115](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-115.md), [CASE-210](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-210.md)'s list of evidence and [CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md) to answer the question's "identify or bound" half.
